Identification comment: 'I know how a customer is identified, the number of the identification and the type it is of. I am abstract: each of my subclasses knows one identification type, the code it is written with in an import record, and how to tell a valid number of that type from an invalid one. I am created through #for:number:, which finds the subclass for a type code and lets it validate the number, so an invalid identification can not exist.'.
DNI comment: 'I am a national identity document. My number is written with digits only and represents a number between 1 and 99999999.'.
CUIT comment: 'I am a tax identification. My number is written as a two digit prefix, a body of digits and a verification digit, separated by dashes, as in 23-25666777-9.'.
ZipCode comment: 'I know the zip code of an address. I am abstract: each of my subclasses knows one way of writing a zip code, how to recognize it in an import record and how to tell a valid code from an invalid one. I am created through #for:, which finds the subclass that can represent the code and lets it validate it, so an invalid zip code can not exist.'.
OldZipCode comment: 'I am a zip code written the old way, four digits between 1000 and 9999, as in 1636.'.
NewZipCode comment: 'I am a zip code written the new way, the letter of a province, an old zip code and three distribution letters, as in B1636BBE.'.
